verdict.rationale: Aider's own documented behaviour stores its output in open, standard formats. Every AI edit is committed to the user's local git repo with descriptive messages and '(aider)' author metadata, and settings live in a plain .aider.conf.yml file or environment variables. Nothing ties that data to the tool, so a user can leave with it. However, no export feature is documented, and nothing covers getting non-code data such as chat history out. Missing for 10: an explicit documented data-export or portability capability, coverage of chat/session history export, and independent or hands-on corroboration of leaving cleanly.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Whenever aider edits a file, it commits those changes with a descriptive commit message.
If aider authored the changes in a commit, they will have “(aider)” appended to the git author and git committer name metadata.
Most options can also be set in an `.aider.conf.yml` file
